knowledge_checks.title: Active Recall: 5.1.8
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. (1) How does EB obtain structural parameters differently from a fully specified Bayesian prior? (2) What premium do you derive? (3) Why is contrast not today's primary?
hints: Use CMP language from today's notes.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: EB estimates structural parameters from data rather than a fully specified prior alone. Contrast LO is tomorrow.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Skipping the LO hinge or swallowing the next LO.

knowledge_checks.title: Checkpoint: 5.1.8
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. (1) Outline the Empirical Bayes move to obtain a credibility premium when structural parameters are unknown. (2) Refuse: 'Computing one EB premium finishes explaining how Bayesian and Empirical Bayes differ in assumptions.'
knowledge_checks.model_answer: (1) Estimate structural parameters (e.g. overall mean and process/variance components) from the collective data, plug them into the credibility formula to get Ẑ and μ̂, then form Ẑ·X̄ + (1−Ẑ)·μ̂ for the risk. (2) Refuse: applying EB is not the same LO as contrasting the assumption sets of Bayes vs EB.
